title: Stop being the last step ineveryprocess.
description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. It offers numerous benefits, including comparing its current value to the previous year, identifying strengths and areas for improvement, calculating revenue per employee, qualifying for bank loans or financing, planning for the future and retirement, and creating a succession plan. Imagine someone approaching you with an offer to buy your business – wouldn’t you want to know if the price is fair or even too good to refuse? Getting a professional valuation of your business is one of the wisest investments any owner can make. Valuations serve various purposes like in divorce proceedings, for bank loans, employee stock option purchases, or liquidation. However, if you’re looking to know the fair market value for selling your business, we offer low-priced valuations. In fact, for every business we list for sale, we generate a Valuation Report before putting it on the market. This benefits both the seller, as it provides insights into the business’s value, and the buyer, as it helps them understand the reasons behind the asking price, making the entire process more transparent and reasonable. title: Progressive Practice Sales
description:
About us We help chiropractors like you achieve your practice sales goals by:

1.) Creating a robust marketing campaign for your practice to maximize exposure to potential buyers. In today’s crowded + competitive sales environment, your clinic needs to have every possible advantage. We:
- Develop a high-ranking landing page for your clinic, featuring gorgeous imagery + professionally written sales copy
- Invest heavily in website optimization, resulting in top of page one search rankings for key search terms. This is a huge benefit as our practices are getting in front of 3000-4000 unique visitors per month 
- Heavily market our clinics utilizing Google AdWords + retargeting ads for each individual clinic

All of this dramatically increases the amount of advertising our doctors are getting vs clients of other brokers.

2.) Crafting a full information package including an in-depth valuation and pricing strategy + a detailed 30-60 page prospectus for prospective buyers

3.) Providing boutique level service throughout the transaction. We not only sell clinics for other doctors; we have stood in your shoes and fully grasp how important this transaction is to you. When it was our clinic for sale, we wanted someone who cared about it as much as we did. And now, standing on the other side, that’s the driving force behind all that we do

4.) Supporting you through the entire sales process. Because we have a very active sales cycle, as opposed to the passive model that most brokers employ, our team invests approximately 200 hours over the life of an average practice sale. The "white glove" service our team of 20+ provides resulted in industry breaking records in 2018:

- 50% shorter average sales cycle than the industry norm
- 98% completion from LOI to close
- 99.9% bank approval of loan applications submitted

HOW IT WORKS: Start with a free consultation. Reach out here, say hi at hello@progressivepracticesales.com or visit us online at www.progressivepracticesales.com Web

title: Customized websites built specifically foryour goals.
description: WEBSITE DESIGN Customized websites built specifically for your goals. Your website is the face of your company online. It is the digital representation of your brand, your core values, your company vision, and most importantly it is your main marketing hub for your digital advertising strategy. As such, it is critical that you display the best possible version of your company to your customers via your website. Book a Strategy Call We Design Websites That Are... We Design Websites That Are... Responsive Responsive website designs are designs that are fluid, meaning that they are built to expand, contract, and resize images based on the browser we detect that is viewing the website. This is the preferred Google standard and we make sure you exceed the required expectations. Accessible Accessibility means your website is designed in such a way that users with disabilities can still consume your website content whether they are blind or colorblind. By adding specific tags that machines can read, your website will be able to be read even by the disabled. Fluid The fluid nature of responsive website design means that all users should get access to the same information regardless of the device they use to read it. Making sure that it responds fluidly to maximize each size of the browser is one of the areas that makes you an authority to search engines over your competitors. SEO Optimized One of the advantages of working with a full-service digital marketing agency on your new website design or website redesign is that we build it with SEO in mind. We make sure to implement all Google-recommended best practices for on-page SEO when we build your website! A carefully crafted digital portal that will be built for education, conversion, or any other strategy you may need. Created for conversions. Before we begin any website design project we determine what the primary objective is for your business. Do you prefer phone calls or form submissions? Do you want folks to chat live

description: Our Core Values Passion Care so much it doesn’t even make sense to anyone else. Passion and drive is everything in life. Be passionate about your work, for yourself and your company. We care about our company’s growth. We care about our individual growth. We care about the quality of our work. We care about growing our customer’s businesses Keeping passion in our daily lives requires consistency Kaizen Kaizen is a Japanese word that embodies continuous improvement of workplace and personal practices and efficiency. Always be looking for potential holes to be filled Always be looking for new ways to solve problems Always be looking for new ways to improve your own skills Always be looking for ways to improve our products and services The only way we can seek constant improvement is by taking pride in our work Teamwork Everything we do, we do it together. Because each one of our team members embodies our other core values of Passion, Consistency, Kaizen, and Pride, we are 100% confident in each other’s motivations, capabilities, and execution. Trust in team Deliver Together Consistency The key ingredient for success in anything is consistent effort. Consistency is about building small empowering habits and rituals that you partake in every single day to keep you focused on your highest priority goals. Keeping yourself accountable for everything you do without excuses or complaints. Don’t give 110% for one week and then give less than 100% on others, give 100% every day! Your best will change from moment to moment; it will be different when healthy as opposed to sick. Under any circumstances, simply do your best, and you will avoid self-judgment, self abuse, and regret The consistent effort allows for incremental changes that lead to improvement over time Pride We don’t want to do anything less than the best. title: Customized websites built specifically foryour goals.
description: WEBSITE DESIGN Customized websites built specifically for your goals. Your website is the face of your company online. It is the digital representation of your brand, your core values, your company vision, and most importantly it is your main marketing hub for your digital advertising strategy. As such, it is critical that you display the best possible version of your company to your customers via your website. Book a Strategy Call We Design Websites That Are... We Design Websites That Are... Responsive Responsive website designs are designs that are fluid, meaning that they are built to expand, contract, and resize images based on the browser we detect that is viewing the website. This is the preferred Google standard and we make sure you exceed the required expectations. Accessible Accessibility means your website is designed in such a way that users with disabilities can still consume your website content whether they are blind or colorblind. By adding specific tags that machines can read, your website will be able to be read even by the disabled. Fluid The fluid nature of responsive website design means that all users should get access to the same information regardless of the device they use to read it. Making sure that it responds fluidly to maximize each size of the browser is one of the areas that makes you an authority to search engines over your competitors. SEO Optimized One of the advantages of working with a full-service digital marketing agency on your new website design or website redesign is that we build it with SEO in mind. We make sure to implement all Google-recommended best practices for on-page SEO when we build your website! A carefully crafted digital portal that will be built for education, conversion, or any other strategy you may need. Created for conversions. Before we begin any website design project we determine what the primary objective is for your business. Do you prefer phone calls or form submissions? Do you want folks to chat live

title: Thunder Armor USA
description:
Overview The Challenge Thunder Armor is a brand-new, made-in-America line of premium aluminum tonneau covers, engineered and built by Thunderstone Manufacturing on more than 140 years of agriculture and transportation know-how (Timpte). The product was ready, heavy-duty, low-profile, no-drill install, backed by a five-year warranty, but the brand was starting from zero : no traffic, no audience, no search presence, and no awareness in a category dominated by established players. The goal was a launch that could do three things at once: introduce the brand to truck owners quickly and affordably, capture the shoppers already searching for a truck bed cover for their exact vehicle, and start building an owned audience and organic footprint that would compound over time, all while keeping acquisition costs disciplined for a business selling a considered, $1,400–$1,600 product. DigiSphere built a coordinated go-to-market across paid social, paid search , and organic channels, with clean GA4 and call tracking in place from day one so every dollar and every channel could be measured and optimized as the brand scaled. title: Scout & Molly’s Boutique
description: Overview Scout & Molly’s Boutique was looking to enhance both the look as well as the conversion rate of their corporate franchise websites. In addition, they wanted to provide a more comprehensive digital offering to their Franchisees and engaged DigiSphere as their agency of record to create a comprehensive franchisee marketing package for their Franchisees to have access to. They also wanted to offer better free resources to their Franchisees digitally. The first step was to come provide a better architecture and visual online presence for their Corporate and Franchise sites. The Corporate site needed to provide much better interfaces for finding Franchise Locations and helping those locations convert more sales when found. The Franchise site needed to tell the store faster and increase conversions of new potential Franchisees. Some of the challenges we had to solve included: • Revamping the locations finder for domestic and international franchise locations • Giving Franchisees a better digital presence that converts more direct sales and directions from the main corporate site • Customizing the third-party Big Commerce e-commerce sites to match the Corporate brand • Providing a better architecture and site layout/design on the Franchise site to be more concise, and direct, and increase franchising lead conversions. • Implementing Schema Markup throughout the sites as well as marking up FAQ pages. • Better Organic results from on-page and off-page optimization strategy implementation. • Better GTM, and GA Implementation to refine is being reported on so the company can make better business decisions and have more visibility down to the Franchise store level. • Providing a corporate marketing program that works for all Franchisees to increase their online presence and increase sales. title: Who We Are
description: Our Core Values Passion Care so much it doesn’t even make sense to anyone else. Passion and drive is everything in life. Be passionate about your work, for yourself and your company. We care about our company’s growth. We care about our individual growth. We care about the quality of our work. We care about growing our customer’s businesses Keeping passion in our daily lives requires consistency Kaizen Kaizen is a Japanese word that embodies continuous improvement of workplace and personal practices and efficiency. Always be looking for potential holes to be filled Always be looking for new ways to solve problems Always be looking for new ways to improve your own skills Always be looking for ways to improve our products and services The only way we can seek constant improvement is by taking pride in our work Teamwork Everything we do, we do it together. Because each one of our team members embodies our other core values of Passion, Consistency, Kaizen, and Pride, we are 100% confident in each other’s motivations, capabilities, and execution. Trust in team Deliver Together Consistency The key ingredient for success in anything is consistent effort. Consistency is about building small empowering habits and rituals that you partake in every single day to keep you focused on your highest priority goals. Keeping yourself accountable for everything you do without excuses or complaints. Don’t give 110% for one week and then give less than 100% on others, give 100% every day! Your best will change from moment to moment; it will be different when healthy as opposed to sick. Under any circumstances, simply do your best, and you will avoid self-judgment, self abuse, and regret The consistent effort allows for incremental changes that lead to improvement over time Pride We don’t want to do anything less than the best. description: FAQs How long does a business acquisition typically take? The duration of a business acquisition depends on numerous factors, including company size and preparedness, the complexity of the industry, and the structure of the transaction. However, most acquisitions take 6-12 months from initial contact to closing. What should I consider before acquiring a business? Before acquiring a business, you should examine the target company’s financial performance, market position, assets, customer relationships, and workforce. The due diligence process should also cover legal compliance, integration costs, and future growth potential. Due to the complexity of these transactions, we highly recommend working with an experienced firm like True North Mergers & Acquisitions. Our team will help you avoid common pitfalls and ensure you maximize earning potential while minimizing risk throughout the acquisition process. What are common challenges in business acquisitions? Without experience, acquisitions can quickly turn into a maelstrom of hidden liabilities, competing company cultures, and disrupted continuity—particularly during the early transition phase. This is why True North Mergers & Acquisitions exists. Our team will guide you through the acquisition process from start to finish, beginning with conducting comprehensive due diligence. We will also provide accurate valuations that consider both tangible assets and future growth potential while maintaining strict confidentiality. Can you help me determine how much my business is worth? Yes, we can. At True North Mergers & Acquisitions, we provide confidential, no-cost business valuations when you partner with us. description: A "Complete Appraisal" is a comprehensive and detailed business evaluation. It considers every aspect of the company and documents the methods and assumptions used to arrive at the final valuation, adhering to the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP). A certified business appraisal satisfies the requirements set by the IRS, SBA, and USPAP. We recommend obtaining accredited business appraisals when the valuation could be contested, such as in legal disputes. To learn more about which valuation service best meets your needs, contact our team. Putting a price tag on your life's work requires more than gut instinct. It demands deep expertise, proven processes, and a partner who can translate your business's unique value propositions into hard numbers that buyers respect. True North Mergers & Acquisitions doesn't just count assets—we quantify what makes your company genuinely exceptional, and we know how to attract multiple buyers to create competition. title: Retained Buy-Side Representation
description: Retained Buy-Side Representation Services Retain True North M&A's buy-side representation team to find off-market opportunities that meet our client's acquisition criteria. True North M&A's buy-side team uses a ten-step proprietary process that includes market research to methodically source and confidentially introduce seller candidates that are not advertised for sale and are a strategic fit for our growth-minded clients. True North M&A matches specific client requirements with acquisition targets. We represent the buyer, and they pay our fee; the seller does not pay for our services. True North M&A is highly selective in accepting buy-side project mandates. We interview the client and only work with those who can articulate a coherent growth strategy, have the wherewithal to finance the acquisition and have a capable team to integrate and manage the investment thoughtfully post-close. Once aligned with our client's growth through acquisition strategy, we run our thorough ten-step process that starts with a highly targeted market search. We focus only on those businesses that meet our client's criteria. We confidentially reach out to business owners who are not actively for sale. We proactively facilitate a screening process focusing on operational capabilities, culture fit, realistic business value expectations, and a growth mindset. Uncovering the best acquisition targets is only one step in a multi-stage process that gets more complicated when market value negotiations and due diligence scrutiny kick off. Our experienced buy-side advisory team helps you navigate these complexities, which is critical to growth through acquisition success. title: Know Your Business’s Market Value Before You Need to Sell
description: Financial Statements Financial statements, such as balance sheets, income statements (P&L), and free cash flow statements are crucial for any business valuation. These statements provide information about the company's revenues, expenses, assets, liabilities, and cash flow. Business Plan A business plan is essential for understanding the Company's strategy, market, customers, and growth potential. Historical Financial Data Historical financial data, including revenue, expenses, and profits, are necessary to determine the Company's past performance. Market Data Market data includes information about the industry and its competitors. It helps to determine the Company's market position and growth prospects. Management Information Information about the management team's experience, skills, and qualifications is crucial to assessing the Company's ability to execute its business plan. Intellectual Property Information about patents, trademarks, copyrights, and other intellectual property is necessary to determine the value of the Company's assets. Legal Documents Legal documents such as contracts, leases, and agreements are necessary for understanding the Company's legal obligations and potential liabilities. Customer Data Information about the Company's customer base, including customer demographics, buying patterns, and customer satisfaction, can help determine its potential for growth and future revenue streams. Non-Financial Factors Non-financial factors such as the Company's reputation, brand awareness, and customer loyalty are essential for assessing the Company's overall value.

title: What is a Confidential Information Memorandum (CIM)?
description: Frequently Asked Questions What is included in a CIM? A CIM typically includes an executive summary, detailed company history, description of products and services, market analysis, management team bios, operational overview, and three to five years of financial data, including Value Drivers and adjusted EBITDA calculations. How does a CIM tell my company's story? A CIM tells your story by framing historical data within a narrative of future potential. It explains not just what the company has done, but why it is positioned for Growth Opportunities and how a new owner can leverage its existing strengths to achieve Financial Synergies. Who receives the CIM? The CIM is sent to qualified strategic and financial buyers who have signed a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and demonstrated the financial capacity to complete the acquisition. This often includes competitors, private equity firms , and family offices. Does every business sale need a CIM? While very small "main street" businesses might use simpler profiles, any mid-market transaction requires a CIM. It is the professional standard that buyers expect and is necessary to drive a competitive bidding process. Preparing Your Business for the Market A confidential information memorandum is more than a document; it is the culmination of your life’s work as a business owner. It is the tool that transforms your operational reality into an investment opportunity. Because the CIM is often the first "deep look" a buyer gets at your company, its quality directly correlates to the quality of the offers you will receive. If you are considering an exit, the first step is understanding what your business is worth today. Whether you need a Compass Exit Opinion ™ to gauge the market or a full exit planning strategy , professional guidance ensures your CIM reflects the true value you’ve built. title: Discover the Market Value of Your Business: The Compass Exit Opinion™ Strategic Roadmap
description: Frequently Asked Questions What is my company worth? Your company's value is determined by a combination of financial metrics (like Adjusted EBITDA) and intangible assets (like brand reputation and management depth). The Compass Exit Opinion™ provides a market-based opinion of value based on current capital market conditions and recent transactions for companies with $10M–$250M in revenue. Is now the right time to sell my business? The right time to sell depends on both market cycles and your personal readiness. We analyze industry-specific trends, M&A market activity and comparable transaction data points, and your company's internal value drivers to help you determine if you should " Grow or Go ." If the market is favorable but your business has "detractors," we may suggest waiting until improvements are made. How do you sell a complex business like mine? Selling a complex business requires an elite M&A deal team that understands how to communicate your unique value proposition. We use the QuietAuction™ process to target sophisticated buyers who value your specific assets, your brand, and the team you have built, ensuring a smooth transition that protects your legacy. How much do I keep after the deal closes? The amount you keep depends on the M&A deal structure and tax planning. We perform a Net After-Tax Proceeds Analysis to help you understand the impact of taxes, liabilities, and transaction terms on your final cash-at-close. I received an unsolicited offer. Should I take it? Remember, one buyer is no buyer. An unsolicited offer can be a useful data point, but accepting one without preparation often leaves significant value on the table. Before responding, it is important to know your Adjusted EBITDA, your NWC position, and the current market range for your industry. title: Choosing An Intermediary
broker_name: premier sales, inc. diane t. thomas pllc, d.b.
description: Choosing An Intermediary As a business owner, someday you will want to exit your business, preferably on your terms. When that time comes, how will you find and more importantly assess  a qualified professional to help you complete the sale? In general, a business  seller should look for a business intermediary who practices full-time in  facilitating the transfer of business ownership. A full-time intermediary  should know what it takes to value, list, confidentially market, and sell  businesses. To help you determine if we, or any other intermediary, are a good  match for you, start by asking a few basic questions such as: "Have you ever owned a business of your  own?" "How long have you been selling businesses?" "What  size transactions have you closed?" Most business intermediaries  will have prepared responses to such questions and they may give you some basic  information that will help you to determine the background and experience an  intermediary can bring to bear in selling your business. But as most of us are aware, responses to such questions may be those which we  want or expect to hear. These  responses shed little light as to how an intermediary will behave with you in  challenging and complex situations where personal motives and emotions can cloud  objectivity. To learn more, you may want  to investigate how the intermediary has dealt with challenging issues in the  past. Understanding the intermediary’s  actions and decisions in real life situations will give you a more in depth  sense of how they will represent your business and interests. At Premier Sales, we welcome  the opportunity to share with you our experiences and approach in dealing with: Challenges at or near a closing and how we overcame them; Potential conflicts with issues of disclosure and how these were  addressed; Representing a seller or a buyer, and what duties do we owe to each;  and Actions we have taken that were in the best interest of our clients  that were not in the best i

title: The Premier Transaction™
broker_name: premier sales, inc. diane t. thomas pllc, d.b.
description: The Premier Transaction™ NOTE:  The fundamental aspects of selling a business seem simple; value the business, market the business, negotiate offers from buyers and close the sale. However in reality, divestiture of your privately held business can be one of the most difficult challenges you as the owner will encounter. The decision surrounding divestiture of your business is a major event and is often the most important financial decision you will make. The stakes are high and the obstacles often varied and complex. Yet ironically, these issues are among those for which you the owner may have limited experience since you may only encounter them once in a lifetime. You may have decades of experience managing your business, but little or no experience with the important and often complex task surrounding your exit. Having an experienced team on your side with an effective and structured process is vital to exiting your business on your terms with maximum value. Exit Plan for Transfer to Key Insider(s) Business:  Manufacturer of Tech Component Parts At the time of engagement with Premier Sales, the company was being sought by a publicly traded company.  However, the company was business owner centric – meaning the company’s success and future revenue stream was too reliant upon the business owner.  Often, heavy reliance upon the owner results in a self-imposed ceiling on revenue. And, in this case, the gross revenue was too low and the reliance on the owner was too much for a publicly traded company to move forward with their interest.  In reality, a transfer of the business, in that condition, to any party would have resulted in onerous terms and conditions unacceptable to the owner. Together, we developed an Exit Plan and put it into action.  This involved identifying and on-boarding a key insider, developing an incentive plan with golden handcuffs and creates two exit strategies.  Through this process of developing a plan, the company and its team have a road map.

title: Financing The Business Acquisition
broker_name: premier sales, inc. diane t. thomas pllc, d.b.
description:
Financing The Business Acquisition Corporate downsizing in the U.S. has made owning a business a more attractive proposition than ever before.  As increasing numbers of prospective buyers embark on the process of becoming independent business owners, many of them voice a common concern: How do I finance the business acquisition? Prospective buyers are aware that tighter credit restrictions greatly prevent the traditional lending institution from being the likely solution to their needs. Where then, can buyers turn for help with what is likely to be the largest single investment of their lives? There are a variety of financing sources, and buyers can find one that fills their particular requirements. (Small businesses--those priced under $100,000 to $150,000--will usually depend on seller financing as the chief source.) For many businesses, the following are the best routes to follow: Buyer's Personal Equity In most business acquisition situations, this is the place to begin. Typically, anywhere from 20 to 50 percent of cash needed to purchase a business comes from the buyer and his or her family. Buyers should decide how much capital they are able to risk, and the actual amount will vary, of course, depending on the specific business and the terms of the sale. But, on average, a buyer should be prepared to come up with something between $25,000 and $150,000 for main street businesses.
One of the major reasons personal equity financing is a good starting point is that buyers who invest their own capital start the ball rolling--they are positively influencing other possible investors or lenders to participate. Seller Financing One of the simplest--and best--ways to finance the acquisition of a business is to work hand-in-hand with the seller. The seller’s willingness to participate will be influenced by his or her own risk tolerance, tax considerations, cash needs and comfort with the buyers ability to successfully operate the business. title: Your Partner For Buying & Selling Businesses
description: Expertise You Can Trust At Van Daughtry Consulting, we pride ourselves on being experts in the business brokerage field. Our extensive experience and deep understanding of various industries make us the ideal partner for both buyers and sellers looking to navigate the complex world of business transactions. Book A Call Now Tailored Approach to Your Needs We understand that every business and individual is unique. That’s why we take the time to get to know you and your specific goals, ensuring we provide a personalized strategy that aligns with your objectives and expectations. We’re here to make your experience as seamless as possible. Navigating the Complexities The business brokerage process can be complicated, but our team is here to guide you every step of the way. We’ll help you understand the various aspects of buying or selling a business, from valuations and negotiations to navigating the legal and financial aspects of the transaction. Committed to Your Success Your success is our top priority. We’re committed to achieving the best possible outcome for you, whether that’s finding the perfect business to buy or securing the best price when selling your company. With our vast network and connections, we’re able to identify opportunities that others might miss. Specialty Markets Expertise At Van Daughtry Consulting, we understand that commercial real estate is an integral part of your business success. Our team of real estate professionals brings unparalleled expertise and local market knowledge to the table, ensuring you find the perfect property for your needs or get the best value for your commercial property when selling. Take the Next Step with Confidence Ready to embark on your business buying or selling journey? Trust Van Daughtry Consulting to provide the expertise, support, and personalized approach you need to navigate the process with confidence. Get in touch with us today and let’s discuss how we can help you achieve your goals. Book a Call

That’s where a business broker comes in – to take the weight off your shoulders
and guide you through the process. Book A Call Now Expertise We’ve got your back! We understand the ins and outs of selling a business and will help you avoid those sneaky pitfalls. Maximum Value Our mission is to get you the best possible price for your business. We’ll work tirelessly to
make that happen. Confidentiality Our secrets are safe with us.
We’ll keep things hush-hush throughout the entire process. But Why Van Daughtry Consulting? Choosing us means teaming up with professionals who genuinely care about you and your goals. Personal Touch Personal Touch: We’re all about tailoring our services to your unique needs, crafting a customized strategy just for you. Market Know-How We stay on top of the latest market trends and use our connections to find your perfect buyer. All-In Support We’re with you every step of the way, from valuation to closing, providing guidance and a helping hand. title: Niche Market Expertise
description: Specialty Markets Expertise You Can Trust You’ve got an incredible business. It’s one that’s specialized, with its unique quirks, its distinctive challenges, and its remarkable opportunities. You need a partner who understands this. That’s where Van Daughtry Consulting comes into play. We’ve spent years immersing ourselves in diverse business landscapes. From the intricate designs of architecture firms to the diligent detail of accounting practices. We understand the craftsmanship that goes into a landscaping business and the nuts and bolts that keep plumbing companies flowing. We’re familiar with the temperature checks needed for HVAC businesses and the electrifying energy of electrical contractors. We know the ins and outs of roofing firms and the corporate labyrinth navigated by franchise owners. Mastering the Specialties You see, here at Van Daughtry Consulting, we don’t believe in one-size-fits-all solutions. We understand that each industry has its own heartbeat, its own rhythm. Your business isn’t just any business. It’s an architecture firm that brings dreams to life, an accounting practice that keeps businesses humming, a landscaping venture that shapes the environment around us. You might own a plumbing company that ensures the comfort of homes and businesses, or an HVAC business that’s dedicated to creating the perfect climate for its customers. You may lead an electrical contractor company powering cities, or run a roofing firm that protects families and businesses from the elements. Or you’re a franchise owner navigating the dynamic balance between entrepreneurship and corporate rules. Tailored Guidance, Just For You Each industry has its own unique considerations when it comes to buying or selling. And that’s where our expertise shines. We offer tailored guidance that considers the nuances of your industry. Our vast experience allows us to help business owners across these sectors navigate the complexities of their specific market. title: Explore Business Listings for Sale in Colorado
description: OUR FOUNDER Christian Alavi Christian graduated from the University of Nebraska – Lincoln (Go Huskers!) majoring in Accounting and Finance and Masters of Professional Accountancy. Upon graduating he worked in a couple different roles at RSM McGladrey and Deloitte with their tax and audit teams. CONNECT WITH ME Having done audit and tax work from Fortune 500 companies to family owned companies on main street, he always knew his passion was small business. Working over 15 years with small businesses, Christian has a deep understanding of what it takes to succeed. He grew up in western SD within the family cattle ranch where he gained a passion for family owned companies.  His professional experience as a licensed CPA at RSM and Deloitte, has given him the experience and expert knowledge of companies’ tax compliance and financial statements. ​ After leaving Deloitte, he bought his first business (liquor store) and has continued to own, operate and consult with many family owned businesses. His diverse knowledge and experience combined with a genuine passion to help family owned companies succeed sets him apart. He firmly believes everyone should follow their passion and be involved in a family owned company. After all, it’s the fiber that holds us all together. Christian now lives in Red Cliff, CO with his beautiful daughter Karoline. His love for the outdoors include skiing, golfing, mountain biking and climbing among many many others the mountain life provides. He is still very active in the family cattle ranch and enjoys teaching his daughter the value of hard work and compassion for caring for animals.

title: Stop being the last step ineveryprocess.
description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. description: 2025 was a financial success and a great year for this business! title: Pet Resort, Upgraded and Ready for New Ownership
description: ← Back to Listings Print Listing → Asking Price $330,000 SDE $186,901 EBITDA Industry $126,901 Pet Services Gross Revenue Location $283,444 Northern Nevada Business Description This established, pet boarding business in Northern Nevada offers a rare combination: a genuinely turnkey operation with the flexibility to be run as a relaxed, part-time venture or grown into something bigger. Built by an owner with decades of experience in the pet-care industry, the business has been intentionally designed as a manageable, low-stress operation rather than a high-volume grind. It's currently run as a family partnership, with the owner and one family member handling day-to-day care and front-desk duties together, a structure that has proven ideal for owners who want a business they can share with a spouse, adult child, or partner rather than shoulder alone. The business requires no specialty licensing to operate, has no paid advertising expense (new clients arrive almost entirely through referrals from veterinarians, other pet-care providers, and repeat customers), and carries a highly diversified client base with no single customer representing more than a small fraction of revenue. For a buyer approaching retirement or looking for a lifestyle business, this is close to ideal: modest square footage, straightforward daily operations, and an owner willing to provide hands-on training after closing. For a more ambitious buyer, there's a clear path to grow revenue through added grooming services and expanded client capacity, well beyond the owner's current, intentionally limited pace. Financial details, are available to qualified buyers upon execution of a confidentiality agreement. Experienced broking agencies like FCBB usually carry out these valuations for businesses. 2. Can A Business Be Valued In Cash? Yes, when a business is sold or taken over, it must be valued in cash, not just shares. This valuation is done by business valuation experts. The agency calculates the value of the company and how much the buyer should pay for it. It is very important to get this right which is why you should opt for our services from FCBB in Richmond. 3. Do You Need To Do A Business Valuation? A business valuation is mandatory depending on several aspects. Let's assume that you're going to sell or gift your business. In that case, you need to have it evaluated to know the monetary value of the business. It also becomes critical if another company wants to buy you out. 4. How Can You Determine The Value Of A Business? Evaluating the value of a business is a complex task, especially today. It can be overwhelming, especially for someone who isn't an expert. There are just too many variables in the market to be considered for people who are not in the broking domain. This is also a good reason why you should approach a professional business valuation agency rather than doing it yourself. 5. What Are The Advantages Of Doing A Business Valuation? There are many advantages to doing a business valuation - ● You can get an accurate estimate of the fair value of your company. ● You can use this information to make informed decisions about future investments. ● It's an excellent tool for creating more value for shareholders. 6. title: Stop being the last step ineveryprocess.
description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. title: Free Market Analysis for Accounting Firms
description: Get Your Free Market Analysis Now Receive a free personalized estimate of the value of your accounting firm or tax practice along with an article with some of our “Frequently Asked Questions.” Simply complete the form below and we will send you a Firm Questionnaire to complete and return to us to start the process. The process is strictly confidential and we will respond quickly with our findings. We look forward to hearing from you soon! First Name Last Name Company Name Phone Email State Select State Alabama Alaska Arizona Arkansas California Colorado Connecticut Delaware Florida Georgia Hawaii Idaho Illinois Indiana Iowa Kansas Kentucky Louisiana Maine Maryland Massachusetts Michigan Minnesota Mississippi Missouri Montana Nebraska Nevada New Hampshire New Jersey New Mexico New York North Carolina North Dakota Ohio Oklahoma Oregon Pennsylvania Rhode Island South Carolina South Dakota Tennessee Texas Utah Vermont Virginia Washington West Virginia Wisconsin Wyoming Email Me the Questionnaire Get the Most for Your Firm The financial dictionary defines value as “ the worth of all rights arising from ownership of property. ” In the case of an accounting firm or a tax practice, most likely the largest asset that will be transferred in a sale will be the intangible portion of the business, or what we commonly refer to as goodwill. But sometimes valuing an intangible becomes an even bigger task. How do a seller and a buyer ever agree on the value of a firm? As a seller considers placing his or her business on the market, determining the most probable selling price (asking price) for the firm is very important. Too often the owner assigns an unrealistic or arbitrary value that leads to a lack of response from buyers and the loss of valuable time in the process. This can cause frustration to both the seller and interested buyers. At Accounting Biz Brokers, we know the market and can assist you in determining the most probable selling price for your business. title: How to Buy with Confidence
description: How to Buy with Confidence and Transition with Ease Whether you’re buying to expand your current firm or looking to go out on your own, purchasing a public accounting firm or tax practice requires a plan tailored to you. Having the right strategy from the beginning can mitigate some of the risks associated with a purchase and will put you on the path to buy with confidence and transition with ease. Phase 1: Locating a Firm to Purchase Analyze your strengths and begin your search. Consider your current experience and educational background, determine the ideal firm size, client mix and service offerings that suit you best. Know what you’re looking for. Assemble a team of professional advisors to assist you with the process, including an experienced broker; a seasoned, competent business attorney; and an industry specific lender with years of experience financing firms and tax practices. Start the lending process by initiating the pre-approval process with multiple lenders, understanding capital requirements, and the process needed to complete the loan. Identify an acquisition by seeking out multiple firm offerings and targeting the right cultural and professional fit. This will include meeting with prospective sellers to narrow your search. Phase 2: Negotiations and Due Diligence Negotiate to acquire your selected firm. Bring an offer of terms that is fair to all parties, addressing not only the asking price but all terms involved including any employment contract for the seller. Transparency and flexibility will yield better results for everyone. Perform due diligence . After executing an offer or LOI, conducting your due diligence may include a thorough review of tax returns, financials, client demographic information, and operations of the firm. title: The Most Trusted Certified Business Intermediaries in the Accounting Firm Brokerage Industry​
description: The Most Trusted Certified Business Intermediaries in the Accounting Firm Brokerage Industry​ At Accounting Biz Brokers, we are focused on providing our clients and customers personalized, professional, and confidential business brokerage services.​ With over 34 years combined experience, our brokers are our greatest asset . They have achieved the designation of Certified Business Intermediary (CBI) from the International Business Brokers Association (IBBA). A CBI is an experienced, proven professional whose claim of competence is supported and documented . With the skills necessary to handle the marketing, negotiations and complex details involved in the sale, a CBI can assist with the successful completion of the sale of your business. We offer a personalized approach to every deal. Our listings receive national exposure and our proven processes throughout the course of the sale have helped hundreds of firm owners achieve the “win-win” deal they were looking for. We work alongside our sellers throughout the entire process. Working together we get deals done. Over $150M transacted Operating in 42 states 34 Years Combined Experience 375+ Transactions Meet Your Brokers The Most Trusted Certified Business Intermediaries in the Accounting Firm Brokerage Industry. Kathy Brents, CPA, CBI Broker/Managing Member Linkedin Facebook Kathy is a life-long resident of Central Arkansas, where she received her undergraduate degree in accounting from the University of Central Arkansas. Upon graduation, Kathy worked for CPA firms in the Central Arkansas area prior to starting her own CPA firm in Conway, Arkansas in 1986. While practicing public accounting, Kathy had many opportunities to provide guidance to her clients as they were involved in the purchase and sale of many businesses. Kathy sold her own CPA firm in 2006. In 2004, Kathy began her 2nd career in the field of business brokerage. title: Producing, Growing Mine of High-Purity Calcium Carbonate & Bentonite $1,800,000
description: Operating with a rebuilt primary milling system and optimized processes, the Company is capable of meeting current market demand efficiently while positioned for future scalability. Its facility includes a Raymond mill, mobile equipment, and tailored infrastructure for reliable and consistent production. While additional mineral reserve land parcels are excluded from the initial acquisition phase, the Company maintains access to these reserves under existing agreements, ensuring uninterrupted operations. The partial buy-in / investment structure involves a phased approach starting at $1.8 million for core operating assets, minimizing upfront financial strain while leveraging operational revenues for growth initiatives. Expansion plans include enhanced milling and bagging systems to meet increasing demand from existing customers. The opportunity is structured to accommodate two distinct participation paths. Qualified buyers may pursue a partner buy-in of up to 25% ownership with corresponding profit share with aligned incentives for long-term growth. Alternatively, the Company offers a short-term investment structure featuring interest-only payments for up to 24 months, fully secured by business assets, providing an attractive option for investors seeking strong yield with defined collateral support. Leadership continuity is supported by the seller’s ongoing consulting involvement, which mitigates operational risks and retains specialized industry knowledge. This ensures a smooth transition and maintains established customer relationships. The business prioritizes quality, reliability, and sustainable practices, aligning with market demands and fostering trust among its clients. With solid infrastructure, dependable revenue streams, and capacity for strategic growth, the Company provides a self-sufficient and scalable opportunity for prospective buyers or investors focused on resource efficiency and long-term value creation. title: Laundry & Dry Cleaning with Recurring Revenue $850,000 SOLD
description: Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E): $550,000 Included in asking price Employees: 6 (3 Full-time, 3 Part-time) Facilities: The Company operates two strategically located facilities on Broadway and 1st Street, offering both dry cleaning and self-service laundromat options. title: Why Every Business Owner Should Always Be Prepared to Sell
description: Blog Home / Selling Business Selling Business Why Every Business Owner Should Always Be Prepared to Sell Posted by Tony Moon January 20, 2026 On December 23, 2025 Why Every Business Owner Should Always be Prepared to Sell Many business owners don’t plan to sell their business suddenly. Sometimes, the decision is triggered by life such as health issues, family changes, partnership challenges, or an unexpected opportunity. The problem is that many owners are forced to sell before their business is ready, which often leads to lower value, tougher negotiations, and fewer qualified buyers. At Peak Biz Brokers & Advisors, we believe every business owner should always be prepared to sell even if selling isn’t currently part of the plan. Preparation creates options, protects value, and keeps control in the owner’s hands. Selling a Business Is More Complex Than Most Owners Expect A business may appear successful on the surface, but buyers and lenders evaluate businesses very differently than owners do. Buyers typically want to know: Is cash flow consistent, documented, and sustainable? Can the business operate without the owner’s daily involvement? Are systems, processes, and contracts transferable? Will the business support debt while still generating income? If these questions aren’t clearly answered, buyers perceive risk and risk directly impacts valuation, deal structure, and buyer interest. Being Prepared to Sell Doesn't Mean You're Ready to Exit One of the most common misconceptions is that sale preparation only matters when an owner is ready to sell. In reality, preparing a business for sale improves the business today, not just at exit. A sale-ready business typically has: Clean, well-organized financial statements Efficient operations and documented procedures Reduced reliance on the owner Transferable customer and vendor relationships Predictable and defensible cash flow These characteristics make a business more valuable whether it’s sold or not. title: Sell A Business
description: Dr. Mark Hagar A lifelong resident of Fort Wayne, Indiana, Dr. Mark Hagar brings decades of hands-on experience in small business ownership, acquisitions, and turnarounds to his role as a business broker. Over his distinguished career, he has acquired and operated more than 20 companies and engineered over 50 successful turnarounds, giving him a uniquely practical understanding of what makes businesses succeed, and sell. His portfolio spans manufacturing, distribution, and service firms in industries including printing, education, military contracting, aerospace, and orthopedics. This diverse background enables him to identify value, anticipate buyer needs, and structure complex deals with confidence and precision. Mark holds a Doctorate in Business Administration (DBA) from Cranfield University’s School of Management in Bedford, England—one of Europe’s leading business schools. His research on small business resilience and operational excellence has been recognized by the Small Business Institute (SBI), the United States Association for Small Business and Entrepreneurship (USASBE), and the International Council for Small Business (ICSB). In addition to his business career, Dr. Hagar has served as a member of faculty at several institutions of higher education, including Holy Cross College (Notre Dame), Trine University, and the University of Saint Francis. He also hosted Your Business Matters, a small business–focused radio show and podcast for more than a decade and is the author of Small Fortunes – the Acquisition Entrepreneur’s Guide to Buying a Profitable Small Business. description: Privately Held Businesses Brokerage Services Everything You Need in a Business Brokerage Team We provide full-service business brokerage services to businesses with revenue typically under $10 million with enterprise values between $500,000 and $10 million. We will work with you and your team of trusted advisors (CPA, attorney, banker, financial planner, and your broker at Advanced Business Brokers) to make the transition comfortable and worry-free. Strategy & Guidance We understand the investment you have made to build your business. When the time comes to sell it there are many decisions to make.  We want you to be totally comfortable in your decisions and satisfied with the outcome of the selling process. This all starts with pre-sale planning and creating a strategic plan that helps clearly define and understand all the goals, objectives, and personal needs of everyone that will be affected by this transaction. Our Key Factors Confidentiality is of utmost importance. As your intermediary, we help control the release of information throughout the process so that you can run your daily operations and only have to engage with qualified buyers. Unforeseen hurdles can take you off track. Our third-party perspective enables anticipation of obstacles to a sale and appropriate resolution of issues that arise. Your story matters. Your unique story along with other vital factors are used to deploy specific marketing strategies to attract the right buyers, maximize selling price, and reduce selling time. description: File#: 225009 Price: $1,998,000 PRICE REDUCED! A rare offering on Mirror Lake, just beyond the Wolfeboro town line. title: How to Sell a Medical Practice — The Complete Guide
description: Chapter 2: What Your Practice Is Actually Worth M&A Insights What Your Practice Is Actually Worth — The Multiples Reality By Platano Advisors · April 2026 · 5 min read Every broker you talk to will dangle the highest possible multiple in front of you. It’s how they win the listing. But the truth is that multiples vary dramatically based on the size of your practice, its structure, and the buyer pool available to you. If you go to market with unrealistic expectations, you’ll waste months, burn out your team, and potentially leave real money on the table. So let’s get honest about what the market actually looks like. The Three Tiers of Medical Practice Transactions Where your practice falls in these tiers determines your realistic valuation range, the types of buyers available to you, and how competitive the process will be. The buyer landscape is broader than most owners realize — it includes strategic acquirers, independent sponsors, family offices, search funds, venture capital firms, private equity groups, and management companies. title: Sell Your Medical Practice in Florida
description: Why Florida Medical Practice Owners Choose Platano Advisors Selling a practice in Florida is not the same as selling one anywhere else. The buyer pool here is deeper, the payer landscape is more complex, and the pace of consolidation is faster than in almost any other state. We live in this market. Our team is headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, our transactions close across the state, and our buyer relationships include the health systems, physician groups, and investor backed platforms actively acquiring in Florida right now. Instead of listing your practice and waiting, we bring the market to you. For every engagement we interview 150 to 300 qualified buyer groups, create competition for your practice, and let demand set the price. That is how our clients have received multiple full asking price offers within weeks of going to market.

title: Know What Your Practice Is Worth Before a Buyer Decides for You
description: Common questions What do I get? More than a number. You get a full valuation of your practice, the add-back analysis behind it, and a written plan: the specific things in your business putting value at risk today, and the improvements that will raise what buyers pay by the time you are ready to sell. What does it cost? A flat fee, covered in your booking call, and credited in full against our success fee if you sell with Platano Advisors within 12 months. Owners who go on to sell effectively pay nothing. They simply get their answers a year early. Will anyone know my practice is being valued? No. The assessment is confidential from start to finish. Your staff, your patients, and the market never know it happened. Many owners run it precisely because they want answers without signaling anything. What do you need from me? One conversation and your financials, typically your last two to three years of P&L and tax returns. Most owners answer everything else verbally in minutes. We do the heavy lifting from there. What if I am not selling for years? That is the best time to do it. The owners who get the strongest exits are the ones who knew their number years in advance and had time to grow it. The assessment tells you exactly which levers to work. Will you pressure me to list? No. Most owners who do this are one to five years away from selling. The assessment is the plan, not a sales pitch.

title: What Top Healthcare Dealmakers Expect in 2026, and What It Means for Medical Practice Owners
description: What Top Healthcare Dealmakers Expect in 2026, and What It Means for Medical Practice Owners Every year Axial asks the investors and advisors on its Healthcare Top 50 where the market is headed. Platano Advisors made the 2026 list , and the survey results are worth a close read if you own a medical practice. The short version: buyers are active, they are selective, and most deals that fail, fail over value. Here are the six findings that matter most to a seller, and what to do about each one. Source: Axial, 2026 Healthcare M&A Outlook Survey 1. Buyers want physician practices Physician practices ranked second for deal activity, named by 51.7% of surveyed dealmakers. Only behavioral health ranked higher, at 69.0%. What it means for you: demand is not the question. There are buyers for well-run medical practices right now, including strategic buyers and private equity groups building platforms. The real question is how many of them you get into a competitive process at the same time. That number, more than anything else, decides your price. 2. High activity does not mean a high multiple Here is the finding most owners do not expect. Physician practices ranked second for activity, yet they drew the largest share of “lower multiple” responses, at 30.8%. The same survey showed wide disagreement inside the category, with some dealmakers seeing strong valuations and others seeing weak ones. What it means for you: buyers are paying for specific practices, not for the specialty. The spread comes from factors you can see and, in many cases, change: how much revenue depends on you personally, how clean and documented your books are, your payer mix, and whether your staff and providers will stay. We cover how buyers sort practices in Two Numbers Decide What Your Practice Sells For . 3. title: Platano Advisors Named to Axial’s 2026 Healthcare Top 50
description: Platano Advisors Named to Axial’s 2026 Healthcare Top 50 Axial has named Platano Advisors to its 2026 Top 50 Lower Middle Market Healthcare Investors and M&A Advisors . We ranked 16th among the 25 sell-side firms on the list. Axial is one of the largest deal networks in the lower middle market. Private equity firms, family offices, independent sponsors, and strategic buyers use it to find and pursue acquisitions. The Healthcare Top 50 recognizes the 50 members who were the most active and most sought after in healthcare transactions over the past 12 months. What the ranking measures The list is not a popularity vote and it is not paid placement. Axial builds it from its own platform data with a weighted formula. For sell-side advisors, two things drive the score: how many healthcare deals a firm brought to market, and how much interest those deals generated from Axial’s buyer members. In plain terms, the ranking measures two things a seller should care about: deal activity and buyer demand. Why this matters if you own a medical practice The price you get for your practice is set by competition. One buyer sets the price. Several qualified buyers bid it. That is the whole job. On every engagement we take the practice to a wide pool of qualified buyers, run a structured process, and create competition for the deal. That means 150 to 300 buyer groups contacted per process, drawn from a network of more than 8,000 healthcare-specific buyers. Axial is one of the channels we use to reach them. A ranking built on buyer interest is a direct reflection of that work. It also means something practical for a seller: the buyers on the other side of the table already know us, and they know our deals are prepared. title: Questions Business Owners Ask Before Selling
description: 1. Business Sale Planning & Readiness When is the right time to sell my business? The best time to sell is when your business is performing well, not when you’re burned out or desperate. Ideally, you want to sell when revenues are growing or stable, your financials are clean and well-documented, and market conditions favor sellers. In healthcare specifically, we’re seeing strong buyer demand right now driven by consolidation trends and a deep pool of active buyers — from strategic acquirers and independent sponsors to family offices, search funds, and private equity firms. What are common reasons owners at my size decide to sell? For small to mid-size healthcare businesses, the most common reasons are burnout and lifestyle change (especially post-COVID), approaching retirement with no succession plan, a desire to capitalize on strong market valuations, partnership disputes, and the increasing burden of regulatory compliance. How do I know if my business is actually sellable? Almost any healthcare business can be sold, including solo practitioner practices. The key factors buyers look for are consistent revenue, documented processes and systems, proper licensing and compliance, and enough profitability to provide a return after debt service. If the business depends heavily on the owner, it can still be sold at market value — it simply requires a structured transition plan where the owner stays on to help transfer relationships and operations. It may not command a premium, but with the right preparation and transition, it is absolutely sellable. What documents do I need to have in order before putting my business up for sale? At minimum: three years of tax returns, P&L statements and balance sheets, current accounts receivable aging report, payer contracts and fee schedules, employee roster, lease documents, business licenses, equipment lists, and existing contracts. title: Wine Storage Transportation Business and 23000 SF Building in Temecula
description: Sold Wine Storage Transportation Business and 23000 SF Building in Temecula The preceding narrative is compiled and written by Margot Murphy, intermediary with Sage Advisory Group. All information is provided from seller and is believed to be accurate, yet all interested parties are required to verify information to their complete satisfaction. NAICS 493120 Refrigerated Warehouse & Storage Since 1982, the owner of this legacy Company has focused on the lucrative and highly specialized niche providing transportation and temperature-controlled storage to winery manufacturers in the Temecula Valley of Southern CA. The Temecula Valley’s wineries and casinos contribute over $1 Billion in local economic revenue to the area each year. This area has been coined "Southern California’s Napa Valley". People flock here for its outdoor recreation, entertainment, small-town atmosphere and evolving culinary scene. Geographically, the area is conveniently situated between Los Angeles, Riverside and San Diego Counties. The Company's owner and founder says, “Over the years, it has become evident that wineries are in the business of manufacturing wine, not so much in the transporting or storage of wine. This is where our Company has excelled.” After decades of service, the Company has built a trusted and respected reputation within the wine industry. The Company’s facility, which is owned, is also being sold. The building has capacity for 1,500 pallet storage. It currently houses 1,125 pallets and thirty wine barrels. Although individual winery customers insure their products, the Company holds a CA Dept. of Public Health Food and Drug Branch Cold Storage or Refrigerating Facility License and a CA Alcohol Beverage License to store wine and spirits. title: | Specialty Label Manufacturing, Automatic Identification & Barcode Solutions
description: Active Specialty Label Manufacturing, Automatic Identification & Barcode Solutions Request More Information Customer Sector Diversification and Established Market Presence NAICS: 561910 – Packaging and Labeling Services 424110 – Printing Merchant Wholesalers 323111 – Commercial Printers C-Corp since 1990. One owner/founder is permanently retiring. Today, there are more and more products moving through distribution channels as manufacturers produce more variations of products—different sizes, flavors, formulations, private-label versions and regional SKUs. Each requires unique labeling, making short-run and variable-data printing increasingly valuable. Industry data is clear. Labels are one of the comparatively resilient segments of printing because they are tied to physical products rather than documents. And because warehousing, manufacturing, healthcare and distribution increasingly depend upon barcodes, serialized labels, inventory tracking and identification technologies, the Company closes these gaps.  For 36 years they have been providing printer hardware and recurring labels/ribbons consumed by those printers. title: Business Valuations
description:
Business Valuations Valuing Your Business Before listing your business for sale, it’s essential to determine a price that accurately reflects both the company’s value and the current market conditions. A business valuation, or appraisal of a going concern, provides an estimate of the economic value of the business or an owner’s interest. This valuation is crucial for both buyers and sellers in determining a fair price, as well as for other purposes such as allocating purchase price among assets, establishing ownership interests in buy-sell agreements, and supporting various legal and business decisions. From Start to Finish Your Trusted Advisors Start the Conversation Schedule a CaLL or Call   (520) 244-1520 Main Menu Adding Value to Your Business Valuation Options Adding Value to Your Business If you’re looking to sell a business, it’s critical to look at the value of the business. But a typical business really has two values. The “academic” value is the one determined by a professional business valuation. The other is the “true market” value. The academic value is arrived at with a formula based on the firms’ hard assets, cash flow, industry averages and multiples. The fair market value also takes those items into consideration, but then considers what buyers are really willing to pay.

For many small and mid-sized businesses hard assets like equipment, vehicles, land, buildings, and inventory may be limited.  For some small businesses there may be no hard assets at all.  Instead, their value is based on intangibles like employees, business processes, customer lists, location and business relationships.

To maximize the fair market value of your business, it’s vital that you capitalize on those intangible assets. Read More Valuation Options There are two primary approaches to business valuations: a Business Broker Opinion of Value (BOV) or a Formal Business Appraisal. title: Recognizing the Warning Signs in Your Business - Colorado Business Brokers
description: Seller Articles Recognizing the Warning Signs in Your Business by Deal Studio on October 2, 2026 A business rarely goes from healthy to distressed overnight. More often, trouble develops gradually through a series of warning signs that an owner may overlook while focused on the day-to-day demands of running the company. A lack of focus, weak management, inadequate financial controls, the loss of a key employee or major customer, outdated technology, operational or quality issues, legal problems, changing markets, and increasing competition can all put pressure on an otherwise successful business. The challenge is that these issues are not always obvious when they first appear. A temporary decline in sales may seem manageable. A key employee may leave and be replaced. A competitor may enter the market without immediately taking customers. But when several warning signs begin occurring at the same time, the impact can compound quickly. By the time an owner recognizes that the business has a serious problem, the options may be more limited than they would have been earlier. For an owner facing challenges, there are generally two paths: address the underlying problems and strengthen the business, or consider whether a sale makes sense. Neither decision should be made impulsively. Understanding the company’s financial position, market conditions, customer concentration, operational strengths and weaknesses, and potential buyer concerns can help an owner make a more informed decision about what comes next. One of the most important lessons is that waiting until a business is in distress can make a sale considerably more difficult. Buyers typically want to see a stable, transferable business with a track record they can understand and trust. Selling while the company is performing well generally gives an owner more flexibility than trying to find a buyer after revenues have declined or significant problems have emerged. title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale - Colorado Business Brokers
description: When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. They need a buyer who has the financial resources, motivation, and ability to move forward. A qualified buyer also gives the seller greater confidence when considering terms such as seller financing.
